items.followUp: Define problem analysis and list two steps used to analyse a problem.

rubric.why: A definition should explain that the problem and what is required are made clear.
rubric.description: Defines problem definition as clearly stating the problem and its requirements.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that defining a problem clarifies what needs to be solved or required.

rubric.why: Inputs describe the information available, while outputs describe the required result.
rubric.description: Identifies the inputs and required outputs.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark when both inputs and outputs are mentioned.

rubric.why: Constraints or limitations help establish the conditions a solution must satisfy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying constraints or limitations.

rubric.why: Decomposition and abstraction are strategies that help simplify and clarify a problem.
rubric.description: Gives a suitable strategy for defining a problem, such as decomposition or abstraction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one relevant strategy and its basic idea.

modelAnswer: Defining a problem means clearly stating what needs to be solved and what its requirements are.
Identify the available inputs, the required outputs and any constraints or limitations.
Use decomposition to divide the problem into smaller sub-problems.
Use abstraction to focus on relevant details and ignore unnecessary information.

items.followUp: What is a computer network protocol? Name two protocols used on the Internet and state their functions.

rubric.why: The TCP/IP suite is a collection of protocols that enables communication over networks.
rubric.description: Defines the TCP/IP suite as protocols or rules used for network communication.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it is a set of communication protocols or rules.

rubric.why: TCP provides reliable delivery of data between devices.
rubric.description: Explains TCP and its role in reliable data delivery.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming TCP and describing its reliable-delivery role.

rubric.why: IP uses addresses and routes packets to their destinations.
rubric.description: Explains IP's role in addressing and routing data packets.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming IP and describing addressing or routing.

rubric.why: Application protocols provide services such as accessing web pages, transferring files, sending email or resolving domain names.
rubric.description: Names and correctly explains one application protocol in the TCP/IP suite.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one correct protocol and its purpose.

modelAnswer: The TCP/IP suite is a set of protocols (rules) used for communication over the Internet and other networks.
TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) provides reliable delivery of data between devices.
IP (Internet Protocol) uses addresses and routes data packets to their destinations.
Application protocols include HTTP for web pages, FTP for file transfer, SMTP for sending email and DNS for translating domain names.

items.followUp: State two reasons for using passwords and list three features of a strong password.

rubric.why: Passwords help stop people without permission from accessing accounts, devices or data.
rubric.description: States the security purpose of a password.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for saying that a password protects against unauthorized access.

rubric.why: Longer passwords are generally harder to guess.
rubric.description: States that a good password should be sufficiently long.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving a length requirement or saying that the password should be long.

rubric.why: A mixture of character types makes a password harder to guess.
rubric.description: Recommends a suitable mixture of character types.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming a combination of character types.

rubric.why: Avoiding predictable personal details and reused passwords improves security.
rubric.description: Gives another sensible security characteristic of a good password.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for advising that the password be difficult to guess, avoid personal information or not be reused.

modelAnswer: A password protects an account, device or data from unauthorized access.
A good password should be long (preferably at least 8 characters).
It should contain a mixture of uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers and special symbols.
It should be difficult to guess: avoid names and other personal information, and do not reuse it for different accounts.

items.followUp: Convert the hexadecimal number (3A)₁₆ to binary, showing the four-bit conversion for each digit.

rubric.why: Each hexadecimal digit corresponds to a four-bit binary group.
rubric.description: States the method of replacing each hexadecimal digit with its four-bit binary equivalent.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining the four-bit-per-digit method.

rubric.why: The example demonstrates the method with a correct binary result.
rubric.description: Gives a correct hexadecimal-to-binary example or result.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct conversion, such as (2F)₁₆ = (00101111)₂.

modelAnswer: Replace each hexadecimal digit with its four-bit binary equivalent.

items.followUp: Use a truth table to verify the Boolean identity A·B = B·A.

rubric.why: A complete truth table must show matching outputs for A+B and B+A for all four input combinations.
rubric.description: Provides the correct truth-table rows for A, B, A+B and B+A.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for all four correct rows with matching outputs.

rubric.why: Identical output columns verify the commutative law of Boolean OR.
rubric.description: States the equality or identifies the commutative law.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct equality or conclusion.

modelAnswer: The columns for A+B and B+A are identical; therefore, A+B = B+A.
